issues.legal_issue: A civil suit challenging enforcement under the secured-credit statute is barred when allegations of fraud lack material particulars and merely restate a dispute about the debt or its assignment.
material_facts: The plaintiff sued for declarations that the assignee acquired no rights under an assignment and that a possession notice was invalid after the assignee began enforcement proceedings against property given as security by the plaintiff as guarantor.
The plaintiff alleged that the assignment was fraudulent because the corporate debtor had been discharged after approval and implementation of an insolvency resolution plan.
The fraud allegations contained no specific particulars beyond the assertion that the debt had been discharged and therefore could not be assigned.
The dispute about the continuing debt, the guarantor’s liability, and the assignee’s status as a secured creditor could be raised before the Debt Recovery Tribunal.
issues.conclusion: The fraud allegations did not make the suit maintainable; the civil suit was barred by Section 34 of the SARFAESI Act, and the plaint was properly rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the SARFAESI Act bars civil-court jurisdiction over matters that the Debt Recovery Tribunal is empowered to determine under that Act. Under Order VI Rule 4 of the CPC, a party relying on fraud must plead its material particulars; merely using the words “fraud” or “fraudulent” is insufficient. The Court relied on Bishundeo Narain v. Seogeni Rai, Ladli Parshad Jaiswal v. Karnal Distillery Co., Union of India v. K.C. Sharma & Company, Ram Singh v. Gram Panchayat Mehal Kalan, T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal, and Canara Bank v. P. Selathal for the requirements of particularized fraud pleadings and the rule against using clever drafting to evade a legal bar.

predicates.civil_suit_challenges_secured_enforcemen: A claimant brings a civil suit challenging enforcement action taken against secured property.
predicates.fraud_allegation_lacks_material_particul: The claimant uses fraud language but does not plead specific facts describing the alleged fraud.
predicates.alleged_fraud_rests_on_disputed_debt_or_: The claimant bases the fraud allegation on a dispute about whether a debt remained due or could be assigned.

issues.definition: When a civil suit challenges secured enforcement and its fraud allegation lacks particulars and rests on a debt-or-assignment dispute, the suit is barred from the civil court.

issues.legal_issue: Disputes about whether a debt remains enforceable against a guarantor and whether an assignee may enforce security after an insolvency resolution are to be considered by the Debt Recovery Tribunal in proceedings challenging secured enforcement.
material_facts: The assignee issued a demand notice and a possession notice under the secured-credit enforcement process against property mortgaged by the plaintiff as guarantor.
The plaintiff disputed that any debt remained payable after the corporate debtor’s resolution plan was implemented and disputed that the assignee was a secured creditor in relation to the plaintiff.
The plaintiff had filed an application under Section 17 of the SARFAESI Act, although the registry returned it, and sought permission to pursue the issues before the Tribunal.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff may bring the available defences, including the disputed debt and secured-creditor issues, before the Debt Recovery Tribunal under Section 17; the Supreme Court expressed no view on their merits.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 13 and 17 of the SARFAESI Act provide for enforcement measures and an application to the Debt Recovery Tribunal challenging them. The Tribunal is to consider the available defences concerning the validity of the enforcement, whether the assignee is a secured creditor, and whether a debt remains enforceable; the Court left those merits open.

predicates.secured_enforcement_proceeding_has_been_: A creditor or assignee initiates enforcement measures against property held as security.
predicates.challenge_disputes_debt_or_assignee_stat: The affected person disputes whether a debt remains enforceable or whether an assignee may enforce security after an insolvency resolution.

issues.definition: When secured enforcement has begun and the challenge disputes the continuing debt or the assignee’s status after an insolvency resolution, the Tribunal considers those disputes while their merits remain undecided.
